purpose: Trifluoperazine is used to treat schizophrenia and helps manage symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. It may also be used short-term to help with severe anxiety that has not responded to other treatments. This medication helps people feel calmer and think more clearly.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical messenger called dopamine to send signals between nerve cells. In conditions like schizophrenia, there can be too much dopamine activity in certain areas of the brain. Trifluoperazine works by blocking dopamine receptors, which helps reduce the overactivity and relieves symptoms like hearing or seeing things that are not there.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, and weight gain are common. You may also notice restlessness, muscle stiffness, or unusual muscle movements. Some people feel lightheaded when standing up quickly, so take your time getting up.
warnings: This medication can cause serious muscle movement problems called tardive dyskinesia, which may be permanent, so tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual movements of your face, tongue, or body. It can also cause a rare but dangerous condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome — signs include high fever, severe muscle stiffness, and confusion. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, and be careful in hot weather as it can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Elderly patients with dementia should generally not use this medication due to increased risk of stroke or death.
typical_dosing: For schizophrenia, adults usually start with 2 to 5 mg taken by mouth twice a day. The dose may be gradually increased by your doctor up to 20 mg per day or sometimes higher depending on your needs. For anxiety, doses are usually much lower, around 1 to 2 mg twice daily, and treatment is generally short-term. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
